_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for roadmap checklist content. Read by both the app (src/lib/roadmap/studyAbroad.ts) and the migration script (scripts/roadmapMigration.cjs). Do not maintain a divergent copy in either consumer. Item ids are stable — never edit after release. Title + description CAN be edited safely; both consumers re-derive copy from this file on every read.

discovery.title: Complete academic profile
discovery.description: Your level, field, GPA, test scores, and budget — the inputs every later tool needs.

discovery.title: Confirm target degree level
discovery.description: Bachelor's, Master's, PhD, or pathway — drives which programs you'll match against.

discovery.title: Set your intended field
discovery.description: Be specific (e.g. 'Economics, public policy track' beats 'Social sciences').

discovery.title: Set your funding situation
discovery.description: Full funding, partial scholarship, or self-funded — affects which schools surface.

discovery.title: Pick a target start term
discovery.description: Fall 2026, Spring 2027, or later. Most US schools have a Fall main intake.

discovery.title: Run your first match
discovery.description: Hit the matching engine and see your initial shortlist — free preview costs nothing.

school_matching.title: Review recommended schools
school_matching.description: Look through the Reach / Target / Safety buckets. Are any unrealistic? Any missing?

school_matching.title: Save 5–10 preferred schools
school_matching.description: Use the heart icon to bookmark schools you want to dig deeper on.

school_matching.title: Compare tuition + deadlines
school_matching.description: Open each saved school and weigh cost, location, and admission deadlines side by side.

school_matching.title: Unlock at least one match report
school_matching.description: 1,000 tokens. Gets you a full AI-explained report — admission likelihood, fit, application tips.

school_matching.title: Finalise a 6–10 school shortlist
school_matching.description: Mix of Reach, Target, and Safety. This is what you'll actually apply to.

application.title: Make sure your passport is valid
application.description: Most US schools want it valid through the duration of study. Confirm specifics with each school's international office.

application.title: Order official transcripts
application.description: Most schools want them sent directly from your institution — start early; it can take weeks.

application.title: Draft your statement of purpose
application.description: A clear, specific essay on why this program, why this school, why now.

application.title: Prepare your CV / résumé
application.description: Academic CVs differ from professional ones — research, publications, awards up front.

application.title: Line up 2–3 recommenders
application.description: Pick people who can speak to your academic / professional ability with specifics.

application.title: Check test score requirements
application.description: TOEFL / IELTS, GRE / GMAT, SAT — varies by program. Don't skip if a school requires it.

application.title: Track every deadline
application.description: Per-school deadlines plus financial-aid deadlines (often earlier than admission deadlines).

application.title: Submit applications
application.description: Hit submit on each application portal. Save confirmation emails.

admission_i20.title: Confirm your admission offer
admission_i20.description: Decide between offers — programme strength, funding, location, fit.

admission_i20.title: Accept the admission offer
admission_i20.description: Follow your school's acceptance steps. Some require an enrolment deposit before issuing the I-20; confirm with your DSO.

admission_i20.title: Submit financial documents
admission_i20.description: Bank statements, sponsor letters, scholarship awards — whatever the school requests.

admission_i20.title: Receive your Form I-20
admission_i20.description: Sent by your DSO (Designated School Official) after they verify your financials.

admission_i20.title: Verify I-20 details
admission_i20.description: Name, date of birth, programme, start date, school address. Wrong info = delayed visa.

admission_i20.title: Review estimated cost of attendance
admission_i20.description: Make sure your funding plan still covers the figure printed on the I-20.

admission_i20.title: Prepare sponsor / funding evidence
admission_i20.description: Keep originals and copies — you'll need them at the visa interview.

visa_preparation.title: Pay the SEVIS I-901 fee
visa_preparation.description: Pay online at fmjfee.com. Save the receipt — you'll need it at the interview.

visa_preparation.title: Complete the DS-160
visa_preparation.description: Online non-immigrant visa application at ceac.state.gov. Save the confirmation page.

visa_preparation.title: Schedule your visa interview
visa_preparation.description: Through the US embassy's appointment system. Slots fill fast — book as early as possible.

visa_preparation.title: Re-check passport validity
visa_preparation.description: US visa rules often require validity 6 months past intended arrival; exceptions exist for some nationalities. Verify with the embassy.

visa_preparation.title: Assemble document folder
visa_preparation.description: I-20, DS-160 confirmation, SEVIS receipt, admission letter, financials, photos.

visa_preparation.title: Print your admission letter
visa_preparation.description: Original or printed PDF. Some officers ask for it.

visa_preparation.title: Prepare financial documents
visa_preparation.description: Bank statements, sponsor letters, scholarship awards, employment letters if relevant.

visa_preparation.title: Prepare sponsor explanation
visa_preparation.description: Who is paying, how, and why they're willing. Practice saying it in one sentence.

visa_preparation.title: Practice with the AI visa interview
visa_preparation.description: 15,000 tokens. Run a live mock with Anna; get scored feedback across 9 dimensions.

visa_preparation.title: Review your interview feedback
visa_preparation.description: Re-read the scored report; rework whichever answer scored lowest.

pre_departure.title: Confirm visa approval
pre_departure.description: Make sure your passport is back with the F-1 visa stamped in it.

pre_departure.title: Book your flight
pre_departure.description: F-1 students may enter the US up to 30 days before the I-20 start date; check the dates printed on your I-20.

pre_departure.title: Arrange housing
pre_departure.description: On-campus, off-campus apartment, or short-term until you find permanent.

pre_departure.title: Pack travel documents
pre_departure.description: Passport with visa, I-20, DS-160, SEVIS receipt, admission letter, school contact info.

pre_departure.title: Port-of-entry documents in carry-on
pre_departure.description: CBP will ask. Don't pack these in checked luggage — keep them on you.

pre_departure.title: Plan school orientation
pre_departure.description: Check your portal — orientation is usually mandatory and may be a few days before classes.

pre_departure.title: Plan arrival transportation
pre_departure.description: From the airport to housing — uni shuttle, rideshare, or pickup arranged in advance.

pre_departure.title: Check in with your DSO
pre_departure.description: Your school will tell you when and how to check in after arrival — follow their specific instructions. SEVIS reporting deadlines are typically set by your school.

pre_departure.title: Read up on basic F-1 rules
pre_departure.description: Full-time enrolment, work restrictions, travel rules. The DSO can clarify anything.
